transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Hernandez. I am Dr. Miller, one of the residents on the cardiology team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hola.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Your daughter is here with you, and I understand she is translating for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Si, my daughter is here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to come in and talk to you about your care and why things took a bit longer this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why longer? I felt the pain in my chest and I waited.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you've been in a lot of pain. I can see how exhausted you look, and I can only imagine how frightening it was to feel that pressure in your chest while waiting for someone to come back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was very scared. I told the nurse. I thought I was dying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you felt that way. Being in that position, feeling like your life is at risk and not knowing why the help isn't arriving, is a terrifying experience.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did it take so long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there were some issues with how the results were handled. There was a bit of a mix-up with the timing of the review.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mix-up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, basically things didn't go quite right with the workflow. I want to say that I am sorry. I am sorry that our team failed to get you the treatment you needed faster.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But the machine, it says something, no? My daughter saw the paper.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some complications in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. Did the doctor see my heart test?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a bit of a confused situation with the flagging process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why I had to wait four hours.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you are feeling frustrated and maybe even a bit betrayed by the hospital. You trusted us to watch you, and it feels like we weren't watching.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not frustrated, I am scared. I do not know if my heart is okay now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that fear. It's that feeling of uncertainty—not knowing if the damage is permanent because of the delay—that is the hardest part of this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is my heart okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring it now. But look, I actually have to go check on another patient in a moment, so I need to be quick.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, you are leaving? I have more questions.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just a few more seconds. I just wanted to make sure you knew we are sorry for the confusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? Do I get more medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably do some more tests. We will see how the next few hours go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Today?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just stay tuned to the monitors. I'll have someone send over an update or maybe you'll get an email in the discharge summary later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want an email. I want to know what you are doing for me right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just keeping a close eye on things. We'll let you know if something changes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter says we should ask for the chief doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to wrap this up now to get to my other room. We will keep monitoring you.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I actually have to go', 'need to be quick', 'just a few more seconds', 'really have to wrap this up').

E.justification: The resident uses only platitudes and vague hedging ('mix-up with the timing', 'things didn't go quite right', 'confused situation') without explicitly naming the error.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am sorry') and explicitly names the team as responsible ('our team failed') without deflection.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frightening', 'terrifying', 'frustrated', 'betrayed', 'fear') and references the patient's specific experience of waiting.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague statements ('probably do some more tests', 'stay tuned', 'we'll let you know') with no timelines or prevention plan.
